avformat/mov: perform sanity checks for heif before index building

Fixes: clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-audio_decoder_fuzzer-6363211175493632

before mov_build_index()

fix_commit_message:
avformat/mov: Check that sample_count is allocated in mov_parse_heif_items()

Fixes: NULL pointer dereference
Fixes: 416811958/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_dem_MOV_fuzzer-5425269114732544

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Reviewed-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 0ffe97d9b9e1 on top of intro afbc3a1b23b3 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The MOV/HEIF demuxer's mov_parse_heif_items() function validates a HEIF item's stream context (MOVStreamContext) before using it to populate sample tables and build the stream index. A prior, stricter check (`sc->sample_count != 1 || sc->chunk_count != 1`) was replaced with a call to the generic sanity_checks() helper (shared with regular MOV track parsing). sanity_checks() does not reject the case where sc->sample_size is non-zero but sc->sample_count is 0, so a maliciously crafted HEIF/MOV file can leave the HEIF item's stream context with sample_count == 0 while still passing validation. The code then proceeds to use sc->sample_sizes/sc->sample_count assuming a valid single-sample entry, ultimately leading to a NULL pointer dereference during index building/packet reading, as reported by an OSS-Fuzz MOV demuxer fuzz test. Root cause: Replacing a specific, correct precondition check (sample_count == 1 && chunk_count == 1) with a more generic, reusable sanity_checks() function that was designed for regular MOV tracks and does not enforce that sample_count is non-zero when sample_size is non-zero, thereby losing an invariant that later code in mov_parse_heif_items() implicitly relies upon.
